fork: carry the AVX1 floor (SSE4.2 + AVX) onto v0.1.37, and make its build path real

The floor's code was only ever on a local branch; the published fork stayed at 0.1.31 + retune, and even
with the code present nothing in setup.py could reach it.

- setup.py: isa_floor_defs() passes -DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=ON to a local HIP or CUDA build when
  STRATA_ISA_FLOOR=1 is set.  The switch is read by CMakeLists.txt but was never declared with
  option(), so a fresh build directory leaves it undefined (OFF) and the engine is compiled for the
  build host - the silent failure this fork exists to fix (SIGILL on the first request, not an error
  message).  Unset keeps upstream behaviour.
- CMakeLists.txt: the STRATA_ISA_FLOOR comment described the abandoned per-ISA plugin design; it now
  describes what the block does (one static ggml-cpu for SSE4.2+AVX) and names the option() trap.
  Comments only - no compiled line changes.
- WARM-RETUNABLE.md: retitled for v0.1.37, an AVX1-floor section (how to build it, what it costs, the
  Xeon E5-2687W evidence, both raw arms), the fork's change list, and the two pre-existing setup-test
  failures so a reader does not attribute them to this work.

Compiled sources are unchanged by this commit and by the 0.1.37 merge: the engine built and measured on
vega (engine/BUILD.json src accbef48a4b25d26, HIP/gfx1100) corresponds to the tree at the merge commit.

Merge origin/main into rel-0.1.31 (PR #390: the layer-split weight carve)

128 commits of 0.1.32-0.1.34 (AMD/HIP, MCP, setup, #340's split ring reserve,
#369's per-layer admission, the pool affinity flag) onto the weight-carve work.

Conflicts and how they were settled:

* include/strata/kernels/ngram.hpp, src/kernels/ngram.cpp, src/ngram/ple_reader.{hpp,cpp}:
  upstream's row-size design is the base (the stride is the tensor's own GGML type,
  and PleReader::open takes it).  Q8_0 is re-added on top as a fourth format -
  type 8, 170 B rows (5 blocks of 34, one fp16 `d` per 32 values) - because the
  Q8_0 checkpoint carries the PLE table as Q8_0 and upstream's whitelist refuses it.
  ple_row_bytes()/ple_dequant_row() are the dispatch; the Direct reader takes the
  variable row, so unlike Q5_0 there is no mmap-only guard.

* include/strata/core/native_dense.hpp, src/core/native_dense.cpp: both sides kept -
  our served_layer_bytes() (the split search's price model) beside upstream's
  keep_unquantized_ple_key().

* serve/server.py: Service.free_vram_mib() and the Vision construction both delegate
  to the one shared serve.telemetry.free_vram_mib(index, amd) - AMD-aware, and the
  same helper the encoder's own footprint reading uses.  The Vision call takes
  upstream's relative-path vcfg + vision_env() and keeps our device=, derived the
  way vision_env picks the card.  The now-unused `import ctypes` is dropped.

* src/program/generate.cpp: our structure (the carve, the ns == 4 placement
  enumeration, the coverage curve, the spill tiers) is kept; upstream's deltas in the
  same region are ported onto it - the SSD keep-alive lines, Verifier::set_commit_async,
  #340's split_ring_mib + Prefill::set_ring_override(96), and stage_room()'s `search`
  parameter with place_with_reserve.

* src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp: auto-merged, then row_bytes threaded through the
  keep-alive blocks that came from upstream (check_rows/open calls).

Built clean in build-v0131.  56 of 58 ctest targets pass serially; the two failures
are environmental and pre-existing (ple_parity wants the Q2_0 shard 2, absent;
expert_multi_test wants AVX512-VNNI/VBMI, which this CPU lacks).  serve's 120 python
tests pass (2 skipped).  Under -j8 the CUDA parity tests fail on VRAM because the
4-way server holds the cards - serial run is the honest one.

Not pushed: the rig builds and tests this first.

root existed only for system prompts past --prompt-cache-every (16K).

perf(deepseek2): batched prefill (blocker A) - prefill 12.94 -> 82.59 tok/s (6.4x)

ds2_prefill runs a prompt chunk through each layer at once: the MLA projections are one MMQ GEMM over the chunk instead of T per-token GEMVs, the attention is one causal kernel (ds2pf::attention), and the routed experts are grouped so each DISTINCT expert runs once per chunk on the GPU via native_expert_grouped reading the arena device alias. ds2_token is untouched and is still the decode path. Sub-chunks bound the scratch (STRATA_DS2_PREFILL_CAP, default 4096); STRATA_DS2_NO_BATCH_PREFILL=1 restores the token-at-a-time arm.

prompt path: never write into the borrowable cache slots while laying out (a resident expert was corrupted)

When serving, the prompt path lays its buffers out at start in the expert-cache slots it may borrow, but those
slots hold resident experts until a request lends them. Writing the MMQ row table at layout time overwrote part
of a resident expert: decode later computed it on the GPU, and the first window that routed to it turned every
logit into NaN ("!!!!" from mid-answer, e.g. at position 138 of an 86-token prompt, even with the prompt read
through the windows). The table is written at the start of every prompt read, while the slots are lent.
STRATA_DBG_NAN=1 also reports the first verify window with non-finite logits and the state a prompt leaves.

setup: recompile a locally built engine when its source changed (git pull on Linux, issue #31)

A compiled engine was stamped only as source=local, so later runs never rebuilt it and a
git pull kept the old binary (on Linux, where there is no ready-made engine, that also meant
no v0.1.12 pool fix). BUILD.json now keeps a hash of the engine's and the image encoder's
source files; on start a changed hash recompiles (incrementally, in build/) before the model
starts, and a failed compile falls back to the installed engine.

Park every session of park-min tokens: Claude Code subagents no longer re-read their prompt every turn

The parking rule took a chat of two turns or a request of 4 x park_min, to keep a client's one-off side requests
(Claude Code's 17-18K-token titles and summaries) out. A Claude Code subagent looks the same - 17-26K tokens, one
turn at a time - and continues, so a workflow's subagents re-read their whole prompt every turn (12 reads of
17-26K tokens, 23-35 s each, in half an hour on the service). Every session of park_min tokens or more is parked
now; the service and run-fast.sh use --park 16 --park-mib 16384 (the oldest go first, a chat in use is parked
afresh every time). README: a live 94.3K-token read from scratch, 770 tok/s, by section.

Experimental speed projection: an optional control vector (EXPERIMENTAL, off by default)

The engine takes llama.cpp's control-vector flags (--control-vector-scaled
FILE:SCALE, --control-vector-layer-range A B, --cvec-mode add|project,
--cvec-dir per-layer|single:L) and applies the vector after each steered
layer's FFN write on every hyper-connection stream: project h -= s (h.v) v,
or add h += d - where the experimental-speed-projection package's patched
llama.cpp applies it (build_cvec after the layer's second combine).

- strata/kernels/cvec: one kernel per (stream, token); with a pending fused
  write it applies it first with the fused read's own arithmetic, so a
  loaded-but-off vector is bitwise the stock engine. cvec_parity tests it.
- Per request: cvec=0|1 on the GEN/GENI line, the API field
  "experimental_speed_projection", a switch in the web app's Sampling
  drawer; a switch drops the conversation cache once. About and the
  Monitor say which way each request ran.
- setup asks (default off; --experimental-speed-projection on|off|GGUF),
  original Qwen3.8-Flash-Next only. The vector ships in
  data/experimental-speed-projection with a README that says what it is:
  its package describes it as a refusal-direction projection.

Measured (bench/results/2026-09-27-esp): off = stock token for token; on
costs 0.2-0.4% per token; mean KL 0.063 on 2,557 teacher-forced tokens.

from "warned and ignored" to the sampled path, and penalty_last_n sets
the window they count over - the server sends the engine's default of

engine's way and omits neutral values; the last-64 default appears

Engine v0.1.2: streaming tool calls, live status, real cancel; fix requests stalling on a full GPU

Streaming
- tool calls stream as they are written (OpenAI tool_calls deltas, Anthropic input_json_delta)
- keep-alives while a long prompt is read, progress in the server window, GET /status
- closing the connection or pressing stop really stops the engine (STOP)

Stalled requests (mostly image turns)
- the expert cache is sized after its slots are written (Windows only counts GPU memory once it is
  touched), so the reserve really stays free instead of the card running at 0 MiB and paging
- the prompt chunk shrinks when its buffers do not fit in the cache, instead of allocating on top
- the image encoder warms up before the engine starts; images are encoded in request order
- the log shows the VRAM left once everything is loaded

setup.py now requires engine 0.1.2 (downloaded automatically on the next START-HERE.bat).

  touched), so the reserve really stays free instead of the card running at 0 MiB and paging

fork: carry the AVX1 floor (SSE4.2 + AVX) onto v0.1.37, and make its build path real

The floor's code was only ever on a local branch; the published fork stayed at 0.1.31 + retune, and even
with the code present nothing in setup.py could reach it.

- setup.py: isa_floor_defs() passes -DSTRATA_ISA_FLOOR=ON to a local HIP or CUDA build when
  STRATA_ISA_FLOOR=1 is set.  The switch is read by CMakeLists.txt but was never declared with
  option(), so a fresh build directory leaves it undefined (OFF) and the engine is compiled for the
  build host - the silent failure this fork exists to fix (SIGILL on the first request, not an error
  message).  Unset keeps upstream behaviour.
- CMakeLists.txt: the STRATA_ISA_FLOOR comment described the abandoned per-ISA plugin design; it now
  describes what the block does (one static ggml-cpu for SSE4.2+AVX) and names the option() trap.
  Comments only - no compiled line changes.
- WARM-RETUNABLE.md: retitled for v0.1.37, an AVX1-floor section (how to build it, what it costs, the
  Xeon E5-2687W evidence, both raw arms), the fork's change list, and the two pre-existing setup-test
  failures so a reader does not attribute them to this work.

Compiled sources are unchanged by this commit and by the 0.1.37 merge: the engine built and measured on
vega (engine/BUILD.json src accbef48a4b25d26, HIP/gfx1100) corresponds to the tree at the merge commit.

Merge origin/main into rel-0.1.31 (PR #390: the layer-split weight carve)

128 commits of 0.1.32-0.1.34 (AMD/HIP, MCP, setup, #340's split ring reserve,
#369's per-layer admission, the pool affinity flag) onto the weight-carve work.

Conflicts and how they were settled:

* include/strata/kernels/ngram.hpp, src/kernels/ngram.cpp, src/ngram/ple_reader.{hpp,cpp}:
  upstream's row-size design is the base (the stride is the tensor's own GGML type,
  and PleReader::open takes it).  Q8_0 is re-added on top as a fourth format -
  type 8, 170 B rows (5 blocks of 34, one fp16 `d` per 32 values) - because the
  Q8_0 checkpoint carries the PLE table as Q8_0 and upstream's whitelist refuses it.
  ple_row_bytes()/ple_dequant_row() are the dispatch; the Direct reader takes the
  variable row, so unlike Q5_0 there is no mmap-only guard.

* include/strata/core/native_dense.hpp, src/core/native_dense.cpp: both sides kept -
  our served_layer_bytes() (the split search's price model) beside upstream's
  keep_unquantized_ple_key().

* serve/server.py: Service.free_vram_mib() and the Vision construction both delegate
  to the one shared serve.telemetry.free_vram_mib(index, amd) - AMD-aware, and the
  same helper the encoder's own footprint reading uses.  The Vision call takes
  upstream's relative-path vcfg + vision_env() and keeps our device=, derived the
  way vision_env picks the card.  The now-unused `import ctypes` is dropped.

* src/program/generate.cpp: our structure (the carve, the ns == 4 placement
  enumeration, the coverage curve, the spill tiers) is kept; upstream's deltas in the
  same region are ported onto it - the SSD keep-alive lines, Verifier::set_commit_async,
  #340's split_ring_mib + Prefill::set_ring_override(96), and stage_room()'s `search`
  parameter with place_with_reserve.

* src/ngram/ple_reader_test.cpp: auto-merged, then row_bytes threaded through the
  keep-alive blocks that came from upstream (check_rows/open calls).

Built clean in build-v0131.  56 of 58 ctest targets pass serially; the two failures
are environmental and pre-existing (ple_parity wants the Q2_0 shard 2, absent;
expert_multi_test wants AVX512-VNNI/VBMI, which this CPU lacks).  serve's 120 python
tests pass (2 skipped).  Under -j8 the CUDA parity tests fail on VRAM because the
4-way server holds the cards - serial run is the honest one.

Not pushed: the rig builds and tests this first.

A prompt read from token 0 is also checkpointed at its first turn boundary when that is 2,048 tokens or
more (--prompt-cache-root N, 0 = off). It becomes the chain's root, which #62's retention policy pins,
so a new chat of the same client reads only what follows the system prompt and tools. Without it, #62's
root existed only for system prompts past --prompt-cache-every (16K).

prompt path: never write into the borrowable cache slots while laying out (a resident expert was corrupted)

When serving, the prompt path lays its buffers out at start in the expert-cache slots it may borrow, but those
slots hold resident experts until a request lends them. Writing the MMQ row table at layout time overwrote part
of a resident expert: decode later computed it on the GPU, and the first window that routed to it turned every
logit into NaN ("!!!!" from mid-answer, e.g. at position 138 of an 86-token prompt, even with the prompt read
through the windows). The table is written at the start of every prompt read, while the slots are lent.
STRATA_DBG_NAN=1 also reports the first verify window with non-finite logits and the state a prompt leaves.

web app: "Use for other apps too" - the Chat settings as every client's defaults

A switch in the Sampling drawer. With it on, Apply stores the drawer's
settings on the server (POST /settings): thinking level, temperature,
top-p, top-k, seed, max tokens and the experimental speed projection. omp
and other API clients then get them for anything they don't send
themselves, from their next request (no restart); what a client sends still
wins. Off again, clients use their own settings.

- Kept between starts in <config>.shared-settings.json next to the run
  config; the server window says what other apps use.
- Only Strata's own page can change them: JSON only (a cross-site form or
  simple request can't send it without a CORS preflight, which this server
  never grants), no foreign Origin, and the API key when one is set.
- Values are checked (bad ones are a 400 naming the setting).
- Tests: defaults reach the engine, a client's own values win, off clears
  them and the file, 415/403/400/401.

Park every session of park-min tokens: Claude Code subagents no longer re-read their prompt every turn

The parking rule took a chat of two turns or a request of 4 x park_min, to keep a client's one-off side requests
(Claude Code's 17-18K-token titles and summaries) out. A Claude Code subagent looks the same - 17-26K tokens, one
turn at a time - and continues, so a workflow's subagents re-read their whole prompt every turn (12 reads of
17-26K tokens, 23-35 s each, in half an hour on the service). Every session of park_min tokens or more is parked
now; the service and run-fast.sh use --park 16 --park-mib 16384 (the oldest go first, a chat in use is parked

Park every session of park-min tokens: Claude Code subagents no longer re-read their prompt every turn

(Claude Code's 17-18K-token titles and summaries) out. A Claude Code subagent looks the same - 17-26K tokens, one
turn at a time - and continues, so a workflow's subagents re-read their whole prompt every turn (12 reads of
17-26K tokens, 23-35 s each, in half an hour on the service). Every session of park_min tokens or more is parked
now; the service and run-fast.sh use --park 16 --park-mib 16384 (the oldest go first, a chat in use is parked
afresh every time). README: a live 94.3K-token read from scratch, 770 tok/s, by section.

Experimental speed projection: an optional control vector (EXPERIMENTAL, off by default)

The engine takes llama.cpp's control-vector flags (--control-vector-scaled
FILE:SCALE, --control-vector-layer-range A B, --cvec-mode add|project,
--cvec-dir per-layer|single:L) and applies the vector after each steered
layer's FFN write on every hyper-connection stream: project h -= s (h.v) v,
or add h += d - where the experimental-speed-projection package's patched
llama.cpp applies it (build_cvec after the layer's second combine).

- strata/kernels/cvec: one kernel per (stream, token); with a pending fused
  write it applies it first with the fused read's own arithmetic, so a
  loaded-but-off vector is bitwise the stock engine. cvec_parity tests it.
- Per request: cvec=0|1 on the GEN/GENI line, the API field
  "experimental_speed_projection", a switch in the web app's Sampling
  drawer; a switch drops the conversation cache once. About and the
  Monitor say which way each request ran.
- setup asks (default off; --experimental-speed-projection on|off|GGUF),
  original Qwen3.8-Flash-Next only. The vector ships in
  data/experimental-speed-projection with a README that says what it is:
  its package describes it as a refusal-direction projection.

Measured (bench/results/2026-09-27-esp): off = stock token for token; on
costs 0.2-0.4% per token; mean KL 0.063 on 2,557 teacher-forced tokens.

Engine v0.1.2: streaming tool calls, live status, real cancel; fix requests stalling on a full GPU

Streaming
- tool calls stream as they are written (OpenAI tool_calls deltas, Anthropic input_json_delta)
- keep-alives while a long prompt is read, progress in the server window, GET /status
- closing the connection or pressing stop really stops the engine (STOP)

Stalled requests (mostly image turns)
- the expert cache is sized after its slots are written (Windows only counts GPU memory once it is
  touched), so the reserve really stays free instead of the card running at 0 MiB and paging
- the prompt chunk shrinks when its buffers do not fit in the cache, instead of allocating on top
- the image encoder warms up before the engine starts; images are encoded in request order
- the log shows the VRAM left once everything is loaded

setup.py now requires engine 0.1.2 (downloaded automatically on the next START-HERE.bat).
